subject: Media Literacy
title: Manipulated Statistics
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Manipulated Statistics.

hook.text: A headline says crime rose 200%. It went from 1 incident to 3 in a city of one million. Technically true. Deeply misleading.

buildup.text: Manipulated statistics use real numbers in misleading ways — cherry-picking data, changing scales, or omitting context.

discovery.text: Relative numbers sound dramatic. Absolute numbers tell the real story. Always ask: relative to what?

twist.text: Both sides of any debate manipulate statistics. Numbers feel objective, making statistical lies harder to detect.

climax.text: A statistic without context is not information. It's decoration for an argument.

punchline.text: Numbers don't lie. But the people choosing which numbers to show might.

quiz.question: What should you always ask about a dramatic statistic?
options: Relative to what? What is the absolute number and context?
